title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Share of Arrears Charges Added Where Coverage Stands Withdrawn
content:
## Collections ruling

The charges for instalments left unpaid on a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record are added into a clearance figure at a share that falls where coverage has already been withdrawn. Two readings decide it: whether coverage stands suspended, and how many such charges stand on the agreement.

| Coverage | Charges for instalments left unpaid standing on the agreement | Share they are added at |
|---|---|---|
| stands suspended | 3 or more | the multi-notice clearance share, 25 percent of them |
| stands suspended | 1 or 2 | the single clearance share, 50 percent of them |
| does not stand suspended | any | added in full |

### Notes

- Where coverage does not stand suspended, the charges are added in full however many of them stand.
- At a count of exactly 3, with coverage suspended, the multi-notice clearance share of 25 percent applies; at exactly 2, the single clearance share of 50 percent.
- The share acts on the total of those charges.

### Illustration (hypothetical)

An agreement standing suspended, carrying 4 charges for instalments left unpaid totalling 320.00 USD, adds 25 percent of 320.00 USD, that is 80.00 USD. Standing suspended with 1 such charge of 80.00 USD, it adds 50 percent of it, that is 40.00 USD. Not standing suspended, it adds the whole 320.00 USD.
